note: Hour-column layout for DPDC's SCANNED zone sheets, read by a Bangla reader from magnified crops of the actual headers and recorded once. This is sheet LAYOUT, not daily data: which cells are shaded is still detected automatically on every run. No free offline OCR reads these Bengali numerals at this scan quality (see docs/SCAN_OCR_FINDINGS.md), so a human reading is the source of truth.

render.why: The grid detector resolves a different number of columns at different resolutions, so a recorded grid is only valid for the DPI it was read at. scan_grid_v1 renders scans at this DPI and refuses if the detected column count does not match the recorded length.

legend.HH-HH: an hour band, 24-hour clock, e.g. 09-10 means 09:00 to 10:00
legend.blank: a spacer column with no label. Carries no schedule and is skipped

verification: Every grid here was read by a Bangla reader from magnified crops of the real headers. That check caught a genuine error in an earlier machine reading of banglabazar (14-17/17-18/18-19 where the sheet says 14-15/15-16/16-17), and found blank spacer columns on azimpur, bashaboo and rajarbag that the ink detector had called inked. Where reader and detector disagree, the reader wins. Two lists arrived with a numbering slip - narayangonj (east) jumped 10 to 12, maniknagar repeated 10 - and both are recorded as the twelve sequential entries they contain, which matches the twelve marked columns in the narayangonj header.

notes.bangshal: The only zone with a full 24-hour grid: 00-01 through 23-24, no spacers.
notes.spacers: Blank columns are physically present on the sheet and carry no schedule. They must be recorded, because the parser maps recorded entries onto detected columns positionally: omitting one shifts every hour after it.
notes.reading_source: Read from photographs of the real headers in which the reader highlighted every column containing a time.
